# References {.unnumbered #sec-references}

```{=html}
<span id="sec-p2-references" class="legacy-anchor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
```

The references identify the works cited in the chapters. The material examined in each work and the scope of our review are described in @sec-source-provenance.

In the source-audit records, page and theorem locators refer to the identified editions and publication years, distinguishing author copies, working papers, research reports and journal versions where necessary. Institutional sources describe the methods or rules at the dates examined, with proposed changes distinguished from adopted rules. Attribution to a particular version refers to the identified text as well as its DOI or repository entry.

The chapters and proof guide in @sec-proofs distinguish our definitions, reconstructions, illustrative calculations and recommendations from results taken from the sources. A citation to earlier work attributes the result used, rather than our subsequent application or numerical illustration.

The two recent aggregation comparisons in @sec-current-weak-order-optimization use [arXiv:2511.19345v2, revised 28 July 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19345v2), and [arXiv:2502.13769v1, posted 19 February 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13769v1). The unversioned repository DOIs in their bibliography entries identify the works; the versioned links here identify the texts examined. Equivalence to later repository or publisher versions is not assumed.
